risks.Risk Description: Risk of cyber attacks including state‐sponsored incidents, ransomware, and data breaches that can disrupt operations, reputation, and financial stability, exacerbated by historical underinvestment and a diverse, piecemeal IT environment.

Risk Drivers.Driver Description: Many institutions have historically not invested significantly in technical IT controls and dedicated cyber security staff.
The IT environment has been built up in a piecemeal fashion with widespread shadow IT, increasing the number of unauthorized entry points.
Recruiting talented cyber security staff is challenging and costly.
There is concern about the potential increase in state-sponsored cyber security incidents and ransomware attacks.

Recommendations: Develop and implement a comprehensive cyber security strategy.
Increase investment in technical IT controls and dedicated cyber security staff.
Centralize IT oversight to reduce risks associated with shadow IT.
risks.Trend Over Time: Remained in the top two risks over the last three years with increasing average impact scores.
risks.Impact: High impact on operational, reputational, and financial stability if a cyber attack occurs.
risks.Contextual Differences: Institutions operating with a devolved IT model and widespread shadow IT face higher cyber security risks.

risks.Risk Description: Risk associated with achieving Net Zero targets, reducing carbon emissions, and managing carbon-intensive estates, complicated by funding challenges and difficulties in quantifying scope three emissions.

Risk Drivers.Driver Description: Some institutions have found it challenging to obtain funding for plans to reduce carbon emissions.
Gaining buy-in from the whole organization for sustainability measures has been difficult.
Quantifying, monitoring, and reporting on scope three emissions is complicated due to reliance on assumptions in student travel and the level of supplier engagement.
Many institutions operate with old buildings that were not built with sustainability in mind.

Recommendations: Develop integrated carbon reduction strategies that secure adequate funding and achieve organization-wide buy-in.
Diversify energy sources through self-generation and investment in green energy supplies.
risks.Trend Over Time: Newly included in the top five risks, indicating an emerging concern.
risks.Impact: Potential significant impact on reputation and operational effectiveness if Net Zero targets are not met.
risks.Contextual Differences: A legacy viewpoint treating sustainability solely as an estates issue versus a university-wide responsibility may increase risk exposure.

risks.Risk Description: Risk stemming from increasing operational costs (energy, inflation, staff, pensions, and student support) combined with flat revenue streams due to capped tuition fees and growing competition for students.

Risk Drivers.Driver Description: Increasing energy costs, non-pay expenses, staff costs, and pension costs are driving up the cost base.
Undergraduate tuition fees are capped, limiting revenue growth.
Growing domestic and international competition for students reduces potential income.
Changes in research funding and government levelling-up ambitions can affect income streams.

Recommendations: Conduct granular analyses to understand cost drivers and income generation on a per-course basis.
Evaluate new income streams and assess the return on investments.
Consider bold measures such as course closures and innovative approaches to income generation.
risks.Trend Over Time: Increased concerns noted in the 2023 analysis.
risks.Impact: High, with potential consequences affecting the institution's ability to invest and deliver on strategic priorities.

risks.Risk Name: Infrastructure - University Estates and Technology Capacity
risks.Risk Description: Risk related to maintaining, investing in, and adapting both the physical estate and digital infrastructure to meet evolving strategic, environmental, and operational demands.

Risk Drivers.Driver Description: A long-term lack of planning and investment in estates has exacerbated current infrastructure risks.
Pandemic-related disruptions have led to a backlog in estate maintenance and required restructuring of campus layouts.
The move to blended tuition and flexible working models has altered space usage and increased demand for modern, flexible facilities.
Decentralized control of buildings has resulted in many spaces operating at very low usage rates.

Recommendations: Invest in capital improvement programmes to redistribute and right-size space usage.
Develop digital infrastructure to support blended learning and modern academic delivery.
Utilize data models to better understand current space usage for strategic planning.
risks.Trend Over Time: Increasing relevance as highlighted by the 2023 analysis.
risks.Impact: Significant impact on the quality of student experience and the institution’s operational capability if unaddressed.
risks.Contextual Differences: Institutions with aging estates and decentralized control structures face higher risks.

risks.Risk Description: Risk arising from difficulties in attracting and retaining high-calibre academics and professional staff, leading to increased workloads, higher turnover, and potential negative impacts on student experience and staff wellbeing.

Risk Drivers.Driver Description: Difficulties in recruiting diverse, high-calibre staff result in increased workloads and higher turnover.
Inadequate management of change and employment issues has contributed to industrial action by thousands of staff.

risks.Impact: Can jeopardize operational and financial resilience due to staff shortages and disruptions from industrial action.
risks.Real-world Risk Events: Industrial action taken by thousands of staff in recent months.

risks.Risk Description: Risk from failing to anticipate, prepare for, and respond to significant changes in government and education policies, which can adversely affect strategic goals and student recruitment.

Risk Drivers.Driver Description: Shifts in UK government and Department for Education policies, including moves toward vocational education and lifelong learning, may disrupt institutional planning.

Recommendations: Engage in scenario planning and proactively consider future policy changes.
risks.Impact: Could have consequential effects on national and global student recruitment as well as on the regional economy.
risks.Contextual Differences: Risk effects may vary based on regional policy impacts and opportunities for collaborative engagement.

risks.Risk Description: Risk associated with the volatility of the student recruitment market, driven by changing student priorities, increasing global competition, and potential shifts in immigration policy that may affect student numbers and revenue.

Risk Drivers.Driver Description: Shifts in student expectations can lead to attrition and necessitate targeting new demographics.
The recruitment market is inherently volatile and challenging to forecast accurately.
Evolving immigration and foreign policies may radically impact long-term student recruitment trends.

risks.Trend Over Time: Although international student applications have grown, home UK undergraduate applications dropped by around 2% in 2022/23.
risks.Impact: Potentially significant effects on tuition fee income and overall financial sustainability.
risks.Real-world Risk Events: Drop in home UK undergraduate applications by approximately 2% in 2022/23.
risks.Contextual Differences: International student trends show increases in Indian and Nigerian cohorts alongside declines in Chinese applicants, indicating regional variations.

risks.Risk Description: Risk that the institution fails to deliver a consistently high-quality and inclusive educational experience, impacting academic achievement, student wellbeing, and overall reputation.

Risk Drivers.Driver Name: Inadequate Adaptation to New Delivery Models
Risk Drivers.Driver Description: Challenges in adapting teaching and learning methods to meet evolving student needs in hybrid/digital environments.
Increasing student mental health issues combined with reduced campus presence make timely support more difficult.

Recommendations: Review and adjust institutional structures and processes to prioritize student support and experience within hybrid/blended learning models.
risks.Trend Over Time: Student experience risks have dropped out of the top five risks but remain the most frequently cited in risk registers.
risks.Impact: Can lead to lower student satisfaction, reduced academic outcomes, and potential negative effects on national surveys and league tables.
risks.Contextual Differences: Differences may exist based on the extent of hybrid/blended learning adoption versus traditional on-campus approaches.
